2609.26034.title: Domain-Adaptive Pretraining Enhances Water Treatment Semantic Representation for Large-Scale Structured Literature Mining
2609.26034.paper_summary: Water treatment research is expanding rapidly, but much of the knowledge acquired from this research remains scattered across unstructured literature. The field still lacks a dedicated language model that can efficiently capture water treatment-specific domain semantics for large-scale literature mining. Here, we address this by developing WaterBERT, a domain-adapted encoder model designed for semantic representation and structured information extraction from water treatment texts. WaterBERT was developed by continual pretraining on a large-scale water treatment corpus comprising about 2.97 billion tokens. Three fine-tuned models based on WaterBERT were systematically evaluated on downstream tasks, achieving the best overall performance among general-purpose and domain-specific BERT models, with F1 scores of 90.12% for multiclass treatment process classification, 79.50% for named entity recognition, and 74.04% for relation extraction. Beyond these benchmark tasks, we further demonstrated WaterBERT's advantages for large-scale literature processing. Applied to 5,144 Environmental Science & Technology articles, WaterBERT-BERTopic identified coherent, diverse, and domain-specific research topics without predefined categories. Building on WaterBERT, we processed 693,211 abstracts at substantially lower cost than commercial LLMs while retaining competitive extraction performance to construct a structured water treatment knowledge graph. The knowledge graph was then integrated with lexical and dense retrieval to develop a Water Knowledge-Enhanced Retrieval System (WaterKERS), which achieved a relevance score of 77.7, substantially outperforming text-based retrieval baselines (54.7-64.5). Through WaterBERT, this study provides a compact and scalable semantic foundation for large-scale information processing and evidence mapping in water treatment research.
2609.26034.paper_summary_zh: 水處理研究正在迅速擴展，但從這項研究中獲得的許多知識仍然分散在非結構化文獻中。該領域仍然缺乏一個專門的語言模型，能夠有效捕捉水處理特定領域的語義，以進行大規模文獻挖掘。在此，我們通過開發WaterBERT來解決這一問題，這是一個針對水處理文本的語義表示和結構化信息提取而設計的領域適應編碼器模型。WaterBERT是通過在一個包含約29.7億個標記的大規模水處理語料庫上進行持續預訓練而開發的。基於WaterBERT的三個微調模型在下游任務上進行了系統評估，在通用和領域特定的BERT模型中實現了最佳的整體性能，其中多類處理過程分類的F1得分為90.12%，命名實體識別的F1得分為79.50%，關係提取的F1得分為74.04%。除了這些基準任務，我們進一步展示了WaterBERT在大規模文獻處理中的優勢。應用於5,144篇環境科學與技術文章，WaterBERT-BERTopic識別了連貫、多樣且特定於領域的研究主題，而無需預先定義的類別。在WaterBERT的基礎上，我們以顯著低於商業LLM的成本處理了693,211篇摘要，同時保持競爭力的提取性能，以構建結構化的水處理知識圖譜。然後，該知識圖譜與詞彙和密集檢索相結合，開發出一個水知識增強檢索系統（WaterKERS），其相關性得分達到77.7，顯著超越了基於文本的檢索基準（54.7-64.5）。通過WaterBERT，本研究為水處理研究中的大規模信息處理和證據映射提供了一個緊湊且可擴展的語義基礎。
